# Step 2.248: a mercy rule and a last-minutes stop clock in one season

## Builder one: what was found (item 1)

Where the pair is refused, and what repeats or relies on the refusal:

- The contract: `packages/contracts/src/season-rules.ts`, `formatIssues` (about line 134): a last-minutes stop clock beside `mode: 'stop'` is refused ("only applies to a running clock"). The same check serves one game's format (`game-format.test.ts` expects the sentence). A mercy lead beside a running clock is refused there too; that stays (the engine only switches a stop clock, `reachesMercy`).
- The settings form: `season-parts.ts` (about line 318) keeps the last minutes only under a running clock and the mercy lead only under a stop clock, dropping the other without a word; the labels say "With a running clock: …" and "With a stop clock: …" (`admin-settings.ts`), and the summary (`part-words.ts` 70–85) has words for one or the other, never both.
- The start-a-season form and `npm run league:make`: `game-rule-answers.ts` (`withGameRuleAnswers`) clears a copied last-minutes stop clock when "stop" is answered (T-428), its test says so, and `stop-clock-dropped.ts` (with its test, the form's `data-stop-clock-dropped` sentence and `game-rules-asked-test`) tells the admin. The script asks only `--clock` and `--mercy-lead` (mercy skipped under a running clock: still right).
- Seeds and the engine's test: to be read in item 2 (`season-rules-reach-engine.test.ts`, in `packages/core/src/modules/games`, lane 2.247's folder: only that test file is touched).

What the engine does with a stop clock, a mercy lead and a last-minutes window (`packages/sports/src/basketball/live.ts`, `clockModeAt`, `reachesMercy`, `inLastMinutes`; unchanged):

- Before the mercy line: a stop clock everywhere, last minutes included.
- After it: the basket carries `mercyClock`, the game's mode becomes running; outside the last minutes the clock runs through fouls.
- Inside the last minutes: `clockModeAt` returns stop (the mercy switch is automatic, so the window wins, S-30); a scorer's own switch to running there carries `lastMinutes` and holds to the window's end (S-29). When the window ends (a new period) the running clock comes back.
- Overtime: every overtime period's last seconds are inside the window (S-28); outside them the mode carried over holds.
- Also, without a mercy lead: a stop clock with a last-minutes window only matters after the scorer switches to running by hand; the window then stops the clock again. The engine follows that too.

The tracker today (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/clock-mode.ts`, `scoring-screen.tsx`): the switch shows the mode in force (Off inside the window); the mercy notice is shown whenever the game's mode is running, saying the clock keeps running, and "Stop the clock on fouls again" always sends `stop`, which inside the window the engine refuses (the mode is already stop). Switching Off inside the window sends `stop`, which ends the mercy's running clock for the rest of the game.

Plan, in layers:

1. Contract: allow a last-minutes window with either clock mode (S-123, decided for you: the admin's choice, and the engine follows both); keep the length check and the mercy-with-running refusal. Tests in `season-rules.test.ts`, `game-format.test.ts`, `season-rules-reach-engine.test.ts` (each phase), one test over the seeds.
2. Settings: keep both fields whatever the clock, new labels and summary words (U-26), keep what was typed on a refusal.
3. Start form and answers: remove T-428's clearing and `stop-clock-dropped.ts` (nothing is dropped any more); a copied season's pair is kept; the browser test's checks of the sentence turned round.
4. Tracker (builder two unless commands allow).
